introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. 0595 COMPUTER SCIENCE 1, June 2020, Ordinary Level / Intermediate Levels. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones and calculators are NOT allowed in the examination room. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D: decide which answer is appropriate and mark only one answer for each question (if more than one answer is marked, the question scores zero). Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Do all rough work in the question booklet.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 1 to 50 are independent; all carry equal marks.
incertitudes: Sujet scanné (CamScanner, filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo ignorés), sans corrigé officiel : toutes les clés sont déduites et les corrigés rédigés. Page de garde vérifiée : Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, 0595 COMPUTER SCIENCE 1, JUNE 2020, ORDINARY LEVEL / INTERMEDIATE LEVELS, QCM d'une heure et demie, 50 questions de même valeur, calculatrices et téléphones interdits. Aucun point n'est imprimé. Le sujet ne contient aucun code C ou Pascal (rien n'a donc été compilé) et aucune figure.

Calculs recalculés par script Python : Q2 (1001000001 en base 2 = 577 = 1101 en octal, option A), Q5 (3 colonnes x 6 lignes = 18), Q14 (2 octets = 16 bits = 4 quartets), Q22 (50 ms = 1/20 s, fractions exactes), Q27 (b = 98 = 01100010, d = 100 = 01100100), Q49 (2 s = 2 000 000 microsecondes).

Q10 (what-if analysis) : clé retenue C (simulation) ; l'option B (modeling) est défendable puisque l'analyse de scénarios s'appuie sur un modèle de tableur. La clé officielle n'étant pas imprimée, à confirmer par un enseignant d'informatique.

Q25 : l'option D est libellée « Geographic positioning system » (le sigle usuel est Global Positioning System) ; clé D retenue car le suivi à distance d'un animal repose sur le GPS, mais l'option A (Geographic Information System) est le distracteur probable et le libellé fautif laisse un léger doute.

Q30 : un processus est un programme en cours d'exécution (option C) ; l'option B (programme chargé en mémoire principale) peut se lire comme une définition large. Q3, Q9 et Q34 : questions de définition dont la clé suit le sens usuel du programme O Level ; options recopiées telles qu'imprimées, fautes de grammaire comprises (« makes request », « all user's »). Q27 : le texte imprimé est partiellement brouillé par le scan (lu « character b is 01100010 ») ; 01100010 est bien le code ASCII de b, ce qui confirme la lecture.

Thèmes : noms distincts de ceux d'ICT et de la Physique (computer peripherals, software categories, classes of computers, file extensions, time unit conversion, satellite positioning...) ; réutilisation des thèmes existants de Computer Science A Level (number systems, data transmission, network devices, network topologies, network protocols, system software, computer storage devices, system changeover, systems development life cycle, programming paradigms, information systems, data security, process management, web page design, wireless networking, computer networks, fetch-execute cycle, data representation).

questions.enonce_markdown: Transmission of signals between the monitor and the system unit is done through the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The monitor is connected to the system unit (through the graphics port) by a **video cable** (VGA, DVI, HDMI or DisplayPort), which carries the picture signal from the computer to the screen. A power cable only supplies electricity, and "parallel" and "digital" describe the way data is sent or its form, not the cable that joins a monitor to the computer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The equivalence of the number $1001000001_2$ in the octal scale is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
To convert binary to octal, group the bits in threes starting from the right (adding leading zeros if needed): $1\ 001\ 000\ 001$, that is $001\ 001\ 000\ 001$. Then $001 = 1$, $001 = 1$, $000 = 0$, $001 = 1$, which gives $1101_8$.

Check in decimal: $1001000001_2 = 512 + 64 + 1 = 577$ and $1101_8 = 512 + 64 + 0 + 1 = 577$. The other options do not give 577. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A(n) ________ is software used to create and modify text files.
questions.corrige_markdown: A **text editor** (for example Notepad) is a program for creating and changing plain text files. A binary file editor edits raw bytes, an equation editor only builds mathematical formulae, and "file editor" is too vague to be the standard name of this tool. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A system installed in a factory turns on a heater if the temperature drops below $0^\circ$C and turns on a cooler if the temperature rises above $30^\circ$C. This is an example of a:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a **control system** the computer takes readings from a sensor (temperature) and then acts on the environment (switches a heater or a cooler on or off) to keep the value in the required range. A monitoring system only measures and displays or records the readings; it takes no action. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The spreadsheet cell range **C2:E7** has ________ cells.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The range C2:E7 is a rectangle from column C to column E and from row 2 to row 7.

- Columns: C, D, E = 3 columns.
- Rows: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 = 6 rows.

Number of cells $= 3 \times 6 = 18$. The trap is to count only the rows (6) or to compute $7 \times 3 = 21$ forgetting that row 1 is not included. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: At what stage in the system development life cycle is a decision made on what type of Input methods to use?
questions.corrige_markdown: Analysis finds out what the new system must do. The **design** stage decides how it will do it: the input methods, output formats, files and database structure, processing and the user interface. Implementation then builds and installs what was designed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The rate of data transmission along a data path is measured in:
questions.corrige_markdown: The data transfer rate (bandwidth, speed) of a data path is the number of bits sent per unit of time, so it is measured in **bits per second** (bps, kbps, Mbps). Cycles per second (hertz) measures a clock frequency, and microseconds is a unit of time, not of rate. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following is in the correct order in the machine instruction cycle?
questions.corrige_markdown: The machine cycle always runs in this order: the control unit **fetches** the instruction from memory, **decodes** it to find out what to do, then **executes** it. The cycle then repeats with the next instruction. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is an email mailbox?
questions.corrige_markdown: A mailbox is a storage area (a folder or directory) on the **mail server** that is reserved for **one particular user** and holds the messages addressed to that user. Option A is wrong because a mailbox does not hold the messages of all users, B describes the whole server (a computer), and D describes a folder on the user's own computer, not the server. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: A folder/directory in an email server that holds all user's email messages.
A computer that stores all user's email messages.
A folder/directory in an email server that holds a particular user's messages.
A folder/directory in the user's computer into which his/her email messages are downloaded.

questions.enonce_markdown: A company uses 'what-if-analysis' as a guide to business management. This is an example of:
questions.corrige_markdown: In what-if analysis the manager changes the assumptions of a computer model (for example, "what happens to profit if the price rises by 10%?") and runs it to see the predicted outcome before taking any real decision. Running a model of a real situation to predict its behaviour is **simulation**. Monitoring and control deal with live data from a running system, which is not the case here. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A measure that will protect files against accidental damage is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Accidental damage (a deleted file, a disk failure, a power cut) is covered by keeping a copy of the files elsewhere: a **backup**, from which the files can be restored. Access privileges, passwords and encryption protect against unauthorised access, not against accidents. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is a network topology in which each network device is connected to a main cable.
questions.corrige_markdown: In a **bus** topology every device is attached to one common main cable (the backbone). In a star, each device is joined to a central hub or switch; in a mesh, devices are joined to many others; a tree combines stars linked on a bus. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software that can be used to improve the performance of a computer system is:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Utility software** (disk defragmenter, disk clean-up, antivirus, file compression, backup) performs maintenance tasks that keep the computer running well. Desktop publishing and programming software are used to produce documents or programs, and bespoke software is software written specially for one customer. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: There are ________ nibbles in 2 bytes.
questions.corrige_markdown: A nibble is 4 bits and a byte is 8 bits, so one byte holds 2 nibbles. Therefore 2 bytes $= 2 \times 8 = 16$ bits, and $16 \div 4 = 4$ nibbles. The trap is to answer 16, which is the number of bits in 2 bytes, or 8, which is the number of bits in one byte. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term softcopy is best described as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A softcopy is output that exists in electronic form (displayed on a screen or stored as a file, for example a PDF), as opposed to a hardcopy, which is printed on paper. Not every "computer output" is a softcopy (a printout is a hardcopy), so option B is too wide. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Modification on an installed system is done at ________ stage of the system life cycle.
questions.corrige_markdown: Once the system has been installed and is in use, changes (correcting errors, adapting it to new needs, improving it) are made during the **maintenance** stage, the last stage of the life cycle. Feasibility, analysis and design all come before installation. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A device that selects the best path for a data packet from one network to another is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **router** connects different networks and chooses the best route for each packet using its routing table. A switch forwards frames inside one network, a bridge joins two segments of the same network, and a hub just repeats the signal to all its ports. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation ASCII stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: ASCII means **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, the standard 7-bit (extended to 8-bit) code that gives a number to each letter, digit and symbol. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: American Standard Commission for Information Interchange.
American Standard Code for Information Interchange.
American Storage Code for Information Interchange.
American Storage Code for Internal Interchange.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following features can be used in a biometric system?
questions.corrige_markdown: Biometric systems identify a person from a stable and unique physical characteristic, such as a **fingerprint**, the iris, the face or the voice. Height, weight and blood pressure change or are shared by many people, so they cannot identify someone reliably. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The set of rules that govern the transmission of data across a network is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **protocol** is the agreed set of rules (format, order, error checking) that devices follow to exchange data, for example TCP/IP, HTTP or FTP. Topology is the layout of the network, a controller manages a device, and a transceiver is a device that sends and receives signals. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The attribute of software stating that it does not waste resources when running is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Efficiency** means the software makes good use of the processor, memory and storage and does not waste them. Portability is the ability to run on different systems, reliability is the ability to work without failing, and usability is the ease of use. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Convert 50 milliseconds to seconds.
questions.corrige_markdown: One millisecond is $\dfrac{1}{1000}$ of a second, so $50\ \text{ms} = \dfrac{50}{1000}\ \text{s} = 0.05\ \text{s} = \dfrac{1}{20}\ \text{s}$ (checked by a Python calculation with exact fractions). Options C and D (20 and 200) multiply instead of dividing, and option A is $5$ ms. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software is referred to as free and open source if it has:
questions.corrige_markdown: Free and open source software is distributed without a commercial (paid) licence and its source code is available, so users may study, **alter** and share it. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: No commercial license and cannot be altered.
A commercial license and can be altered.
No commercial license and can be altered.
A commercial license and cannot be altered.

questions.enonce_markdown: Sending a file from your computer to a server is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Copying a file from your computer to a remote server is **uploading**; the opposite direction (server to your computer) is downloading. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is a technology that can be used to locate an elephant remotely in a forest.
questions.corrige_markdown: An animal can be located remotely by fitting it with a collar that uses satellite positioning (GPS) to find its position and sends it back to the researchers. Option D is the positioning system (GPS). A Geographic Information System (A) stores, analyses and maps location data but does not find the position of the animal by itself, "Location Information System" (B) is not a standard technology, and a transmitter (C) only sends signals. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Communication on cell phone is an example of ________ communication.
questions.corrige_markdown: On a cell phone both people can talk and listen at the same time, so data flows in both directions simultaneously: **full duplex**. Simplex is one direction only (radio broadcast) and half duplex is two directions but one at a time (walkie-talkie). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The binary code for ASCII character b is 01100010. What is the binary code for ASCII character d?
questions.corrige_markdown: In ASCII the letters follow each other in alphabetical order, so d is two codes after b. The code of b is $01100010_2 = 98$, therefore d $= 98 + 2 = 100 = 01100100_2$ (checked with Python: `format(100, '08b')` gives 01100100). The other options are the codes of m (01101101), j (01101010) and l (01101100). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a typical Client-Server network:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the client-server model the **client** asks (makes a request) and the **server** answers by providing the resource (a web page, a file, a mail message). Options A, C and D reverse these roles. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the server computer initiates all communication.
the client computer makes request for resources.
the server computer makes request for resources.
the client computer provides needed resources.

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation FTP stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: FTP is the **File Transfer Protocol**, used to upload and download files between computers on a network. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the functions of an operating system in a computer is to manage processes. The term process refers to a:
questions.corrige_markdown: A process is a **program in execution**: the running instance of a program, with the CPU executing its instructions. A program only stored on the hard disk (A) or compiled and waiting (D) is not yet a process, and a program loaded in main memory (B) is only waiting unless the CPU is executing it. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The HTML open and close tags
    ---
are used to generate:
questions.corrige_markdown: `<ul>` means *unordered list*: each `<li>` item inside it is shown with a bullet. A numbered list uses `<ol>` (ordered list), and underlined text uses `<u>`. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation USB stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: USB stands for **Universal Serial Bus**, the standard port and cable used to connect peripherals such as keyboards, flash drives and phones. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A system designed to track daily sales and purchases of a company is a(n) ________ system.
questions.corrige_markdown: Recording every day-to-day sale and purchase as it happens is the job of a **transaction processing system** (TPS). Management information, decision support and executive information systems work on summaries of this data to help managers decide. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is true about user name and passwords in an information system?
questions.corrige_markdown: The user name identifies the account, so it must be **unique**; the password is only a secret that proves identity, so two users may happen to choose the same one. Option A reverses this, and a password change does not require a new user name (D). Changing a user name (C) would create a different identity and is not a general rule. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Users can have the same user name, but their passwords must be different.
Users can have the same password, but their user names must be different.
Users are able to change their user names and still have access to their account.
When users change their passwords, they must also change their user names.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following is NOT a component of an information system?
questions.corrige_markdown: The components of an information system are hardware, software, data, people (users) and procedures. A **computer table** is furniture, not a component of the system. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is a programming paradigm that specifies a problem to be solved but does not specify how to solve it.
questions.corrige_markdown: In **declarative** programming (SQL, Prolog, HTML) the programmer states *what* result is wanted and the system works out how to get it. Procedural and imperative programming give the step-by-step instructions (*how*), and object-oriented programming organises the program into objects. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is usually described as a knowledge-based system.
questions.corrige_markdown: An **expert system** contains a knowledge base of facts and rules from human experts and an inference engine that uses them to give advice or diagnoses (for example medical diagnosis). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In system implementation, parallel conversion means:
questions.corrige_markdown: In **parallel** conversion both systems run together for a period, so the results can be compared and the old system is a safe fall-back if the new one fails. Option B describes pilot running, C is phased conversion, and D is direct (abrupt) changeover. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: running the new system alongside the old system.
running some parts of the new system alongside the old system.
replacing parts of the old system with parts of the new system.
running the new system while the old one is shut down.

questions.enonce_markdown: When an email message is sent from John to Mary, copies of the message are found in:
questions.corrige_markdown: The sender keeps a copy in the **Sent** folder, and the recipient receives the message in the **Inbox**. So the copies are in John's sent folder and Mary's inbox folder. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: John's sent folder and Mary's inbox folder.
John's sent folder and his inbox to Mary on a server.
Mary's sent folder and John's inbox folder.
a folder's inbox folder and Mary sent folder on a server.

questions.enonce_markdown: The file extension .pdf stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: PDF means **Portable Document Format**: a file format that keeps the layout of a document the same on any device. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Flash memory is an example of a(n) ________ storage device.
questions.corrige_markdown: Flash memory has no moving parts and stores data in electronic circuits, so it is a **solid state** device (flash drives, memory cards, SSDs). Optical devices use a laser (CD, DVD) and magnetic devices use magnetised surfaces (hard disk). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Disk compression software is a type of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Disk compression reduces the space taken by files on a disk. It is a maintenance tool for the computer itself, so it is **utility software**. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT an example of a storage device?
questions.corrige_markdown: Flash memory, ROM chips and hard disks all hold data. The **CPU** processes data; it is not a storage device. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software that enables an operating system to communicate effectively with a given peripheral device is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **device driver** translates the operating system's commands into the commands that a particular peripheral (printer, scanner, graphics card) understands. A firewall filters network traffic, bespoke software is custom-made software, and a widget is a small on-screen tool. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ system enables people who are geographically dispersed to have an online meeting that looks like a real life situation.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Videoconferencing** lets people in different places see and hear each other live, like a face-to-face meeting. Electronic marketing is advertising online, MMS sends recorded messages, and teleworking means working remotely. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In project management, lag time means a delay between:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a project network, tasks are linked as predecessor (comes first) and successor (comes after). The waiting time between the end of the predecessor and the start of the successor is the **lag time**. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: a predecessor and a successor task.

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is a class of computers that is most suitable for weaponry and weather forecasting.
questions.corrige_markdown: Weather forecasting and weapons simulation need enormous numbers of calculations at great speed, which only a **supercomputer** can do. Minicomputers, microcomputers and laptops are much less powerful. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Communication between a hand held remote controller and a television set is an example of ________ communication.
questions.corrige_markdown: A television remote control sends pulses of **infrared** light to the sensor of the television; it works in line of sight over a short distance. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Convert 2 seconds to microseconds.
questions.corrige_markdown: One second is $10^6$ microseconds ($1\ \mu\text{s} = 10^{-6}\ \text{s}$), so $2\ \text{s} = 2 \times 10^6\ \mu\text{s} = 2\,000\,000\ \mu\text{s}$ (checked with Python). Option A is 2 seconds in milliseconds, and options C and D divide instead of multiplying. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ergonomics is concerned about:
questions.corrige_markdown: Ergonomics studies how to design and arrange the workplace (chair, desk, screen, keyboard, lighting) so that users work comfortably, safely and without health problems. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the economies of writing and displaying characters.
the design of pictures and word art.
the design and placement of equipment in a computer workplace.
speed and accuracy of a computer user.
